title: RAG Post Processor
description: Clean and chunk scraped text into embedding-ready chunks, sized in tokens and split on document structure.

datasetId.title: Dataset ID (for chaining)
datasetId.description: Apify dataset ID from a previous Actor run. Use this to chain directly after any scraper. All pages are read, not just the first.

data.title: Input items
data.description: Array of objects from a previous scraper. Each needs a text field — markdown, text, content, body, html and around 25 other common names are recognised automatically.

text_field.title: Text field name
text_field.description: Name the field to read instead of relying on automatic detection. Useful when your scraper uses a custom field name, or when an item has several text fields and you want a specific one. The field actually used is reported on every output row as source_field.

max_tokens.title: Max tokens per chunk
max_tokens.sectionDescription: Budgets are in tokens, not characters, because tokens are what embedding models limit on and charge for. The same 1000-character chunk is roughly 160 tokens of English and 1080 tokens of Japanese.
max_tokens.description: Hard ceiling on tokens per chunk, measured with the encoding below. No emitted chunk ever exceeds this. 8191 is the input limit for OpenAI's text-embedding-3 models.

overlap_tokens.title: Overlap between chunks (tokens)
overlap_tokens.description: Tokens of trailing context repeated at the start of the next chunk. Only whole sentences are carried, so a chunk never begins mid-word. Clamped to 50% of max_tokens; 50% is fully supported. Overlap duplicates tokens, and the run log reports the resulting amplification so you can budget your embedding spend.

min_tokens.title: Minimum tokens per chunk
min_tokens.description: Chunks below this are merged into the previous chunk rather than emitted as their own row. No text is ever dropped.

encoding.title: Tokenizer encoding
encoding.description: Which tokenizer to measure with. Pick the one your embedding model uses. Note that text-embedding-3-small and -large use cl100k_base, not o200k_base, despite being newer models. The BPE tables are bundled into the image, so no download happens at run time.

split_on_heading_level.title: Force a new chunk at heading level
split_on_heading_level.sectionDescription: Chunks are built from document blocks — headings, paragraphs, fenced code, tables and lists — rather than by slicing a character stream. Code that must be split keeps its fence and language on every part, and a split table repeats its header row, so each chunk is still interpretable on its own after retrieval.
split_on_heading_level.description: 0 packs sections together to fill the budget. Set 1 to 6 to start a new chunk at every heading of that level or higher, so one section never bleeds into the next. Use 2 for typical documentation pages.

include_heading_context.title: Prefix chunks with their heading path
include_heading_context.description: Prepend the breadcrumb (for example "Widget SDK > Quick start") to each chunk's text, so an isolated passage still carries the context a retriever needs. The path is also emitted separately as heading_path and section on every row.

preserve_links.title: Keep URLs and links
preserve_links.description: Keep URLs in the text and convert HTML anchors to markdown links, so retrieved passages can still be cited. Turn off only if you want URLs stripped entirely.

drop_nav.title: Drop navigation chrome
drop_nav.description: Remove nav and menu contents. Script, style, noscript, template, svg and comment contents are always removed.
